title: Context residency manifest and pinbook for per-model KV behavior
creator: Sanjay Rao
description:
Problem: We lack a compact, versioned artifact that captures per-model long-context "residency" characteristics (how often sequences keep KV alive across requests, tail sequence lengths, and session hotness). Without this manifest we make conservative pinning choices that increase memory pressure or aggressive evictions that regress latency for long-session customers.

Goal: Define and publish a 'context residency manifest' and an associated 'pinbook' which together guide model-version pinning, KV retention TTLs, and warmup heuristics. The manifest must be machine-readable, versioned, and small enough to ship with model metadata. The pinbook is an internal decision document mapping residency signals to pin/evict policies and fallback variants.
acceptance_criteria:
- A JSON residency manifest schema is defined and checked into runtime/manifest-specs.
- Residency extractor job produces manifests for 5 canonical models (including at least one long-sequence LLM) and they are visible in the model catalog.
- Automations map manifest fields to pinbook recommendations (TTL, pin affinity, warmup priority).
- Can run a 2-week canary where 10% of traffic uses manifest-driven pinning; no more than 5% latency p50 regression on affected routes.
- Ops runbook added to Console explaining manifest rollout and manual override steps.
implementation_notes:
Design components: (1) Residency signature: per-model sequence-length histogram, session re-hit rate, median inter-arrival for reused KV anchors, and a compact 'residency score' in 3 buckets (LOW/MED/HIGH). (2) Manifest fields: model_id, manifest_version, generated_at, seq_histogram_quantiles (p50,p90,p99), anchor_reuse_rate, avg_kv_lifetime_ms, residency_score, suggested_ttl_ms, recommended_pin_variant. (3) Extraction pipeline: sample production traces daily with privacy-preserving sampling, produce sequence-anchored histograms and compute residency score. (4) Pinbook mapping: mapping from residency_score + memory_budget -> pin decision and warmup priority.

Trade-offs considered:
- Granularity vs size: we prefer quantiles to full distributions to keep manifests small.
- Conservative defaults for stability: manifest-driven pins are recommendations; runtime keeps safety caps.
- Privacy: only aggregated histograms leave the pipeline; no raw PII traces persist.

Edge cases: anchorless sessions (single-request long sequences) should set suggested_ttl_ms low and warmup priority zero. Multi-client fanout patterns should surface as high avg_kv_lifetime_ms but low anchor_reuse_rate and be treated as MED residency.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (week 1-2): design schema + unit tests; produce manifests for internal benchmark models and publish to staging catalog. Phase 2 (week 3): add runtime mappings from manifest to TTL and pin recommendations behind a feature flag. Phase 3 (week 4): enable for 10% traffic on non-critical routes for 14 days; monitor latency, OOMs, and KV hit-rate. Phase 4 (week 6): expand to 50% traffic and onboard 3 additional models. Final: graduate to default policy and include manifest in model onboarding checklist.

Rollback criteria: any sustained p50 increase >5% on flagged routes or >2 unexpected OOM incidents attributable to pinning within the canary window.
metrics: Primary: per-route p50/p95 latency delta (manifest vs baseline), KV hit-rate delta, average KV memory utilization per model, frequency of pin fallbacks triggered. Secondary: manifest generation success rate, drift detection rate (manifests deviating >20% from live telemetry). All metrics must be visible on the 'kvcache-residency-overview' dashboard.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for manifest schema validation and backward compatibility.
- Synthetic load tests with long-sequence generators to validate TTL behavior.
- Regression test: compare baseline warmup vs manifest-driven warmup for throughput and latency under burst traffic.
- Privacy test: end-to-end check that only aggregated quantiles leave extraction job.
- Canary: 10% traffic A/B for 14 days with automated alerts for rollback thresholds.
notes:
Implementation will reuse sequence-sampler from ENG-62789 and the pin orchestration API added in ENG-51230. We will add a compact 'manifest_version' field to model metadata in the catalog to allow safe rollbacks and forced pin overrides from Console.

Requesting review from: Product (Maya Chen) for customer impact alignment, Observability (Owen Park) for dashboard slices, Security (Aisha Malik) to confirm privacy constraints.

Posterior work: build a small 'manifest diff' notifier that flags manifests whose p90 or anchor_reuse_rate shifts >25% week-over-week (future ticket).
